clue.text: Exclusive control of game

definitions.meaning: sole command of a market or supply, with no competitor
the property-trading board game with houses and hotels

explanation.surface: Someone insists on running the game all by themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses share one word: an economist's term for sole market power, and the famous board game of buying streets.

clue.text: Cat climbing round boy to annoy

indicators.note: the reversed cat goes around the boy's name
in a down clue climbing means the word reads upwards, so backwards

parts.note: a tom is a male cat
Les is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A cat climbs around a boy to pester him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climbing' reverses the cat to MOT, which 'round' wraps about the boy's name. In a down clue, climbing means reading from the bottom up.
explanation.definitionFit: To molest in the older sense is to pester or harass someone.

clue.text: Scottish island rising made into story

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means the word reads upwards, from the bottom

parts.note: Arran is an island in the Firth of Clyde

indicators.note: the word into is made over, its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A Scottish island's rise is turned into a tale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' turns ARRAN into NARRA; 'made' rearranges INTO as TION.
explanation.definitionFit: A narration is an account or telling of events.

clue.text: A: prison riot can't be affected by delay

indicators.note: letters that are affected are disturbed, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A jail riot cannot be influenced by stalling tactics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'be affected' rearranges A PRISON RIOT CANT; 'by' links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Putting things off, stalling and postponing, is a form of deferral.

clue.text: Apprentice under a new stupid person

parts.note: L is for learner, as on an apprentice driver's plate

indicators.note: a new version of the words gives their letters in a fresh order

explanation.surface: A trainee working under a newcomer is a dimwit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges UNDER A into URDANE; the learner sits on top, matching 'under' in the surface only.
explanation.definitionFit: Lurdane is an archaic word for an idle, dull-witted lout.

clue.text: Trip: is difficult so show courage

indicators.note: the letters of the two words are made awkward and rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: A tough journey calls for bravery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'difficult' rearranges the letters of TRIP and IS; 'so show' only links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Spirit is pluck or mettle, the boldness to face danger.

clue.text: Celebrated with noted parent getting drunk

indicators.note: drunken letters stagger into a new order

explanation.surface: A famous father got drunk while partying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting drunk' rearranges WITH NOTED PARENT. 'Celebrated' looks like 'famous' beside 'noted', but it is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To go out on a riotous night of revelry is to party hard, celebrating lavishly.

clue.text: One up?

parts.note: up means mounted on a horse, so this is someone in the saddle, not a person ahead in a game

explanation.surface: Who is leading?
explanation.definitionFit: A jockey or horseman is said to be up when mounted.

clue.text: Here, don't compose a sad song

indicators.note: to compose is to put together, so these letters are assembled anew

explanation.surface: Someone is told not to write a mournful tune here.
explanation.definitionFit: A threnody or threnode is a lament or dirge for the dead.

clue.text: A doctor with English graduate discovers protozoon

parts.note: MO is a medical officer, an army doctor
BA is Bachelor of Arts, a graduate

explanation.surface: A doctor and an English graduate find a single-celled organism.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' and 'discovers' only link.
explanation.definitionFit: The amoeba is a single-celled organism of the protozoa group.

clue.text: Broad and slow number join Jason's ship

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty
the Argo carried Jason and the Argonauts in Greek myth

explanation.surface: A slow, broad piece of music is invited to board a legendary vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'join' just links the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: In musical directions the Italian tempo marking means played broadly and at a slow pace.

clue.text: Stay with the German to get what's left

parts.note: to stay is to remain
der is a German word for 'the'

explanation.surface: Someone stays on with a German companion to collect the leftovers.
explanation.definitionFit: The remainder is the leftover part once the rest is taken away.

clue.text: A caster is moulded to help one up and down

indicators.note: moulding reshapes material, so the letters are reformed into a different order

explanation.surface: A wheel or castor is cast in a mould to help someone move.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram uses all of A CASTER IS, including the 'is' that also reads as part of the indicator phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: A flight of steps lets a person climb to a higher floor and come back down.

clue.text: I enter act in Italy

indicators.note: the single letter goes into the word for an act

parts.note: a turn is a stage act, as in a music-hall turn

explanation.surface: Someone takes part in a performance while in Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: Turin is a city located in north-west Italy, the Piedmont capital.

clue.text: The first publication having, thin paper

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word 'The' is taken

parts.note: an issue is one published edition of a magazine or paper

explanation.surface: The debut edition of a magazine was printed on flimsy paper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having' only links the pieces to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Tissue is soft, very fine paper used for wrapping or handkerchiefs.

clue.text: Embarrassed a bogus journalist

parts.note: a sham is a fake, so bogus gives sham
ED is short for editor, a journalist in crosswords

explanation.surface: A reporter was shown up as a fraud and felt mortified.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling shame or awkwardness about something you did is to be mortified.

clue.text: Disorder at headless monument in Sicily

indicators.note: putting letters into disorder jumbles them
the word monument loses its first letter

explanation.surface: Unrest breaks out at a damaged monument in Sicily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'headless' cuts MONUMENT to ONUMENT; 'Disorder' rearranges that with AT.
explanation.definitionFit: The great volcano dominates the east of the Italian island.

clue.text: Like going round tin hut maybe to see shrub

indicators.note: the word for like goes around the other pieces

parts.note: as means like
a can is a tin

indicators.note: maybe signals a possible rearrangement of the letters

explanation.surface: A tin hut is visited to look at a bush.
explanation.walkthrough: 'maybe' rearranges the hut's letters; 'going round' puts the tin and that anagram inside the word for like. The printed page reads 'tin hut', not 'tin but'.
explanation.definitionFit: Acanthus is a Mediterranean plant with spiny leaves, the model for Corinthian capitals.

clue.text: Verify study is by company

parts.note: to con is an old word meaning to study or learn by heart
a firm is a business company

explanation.surface: A company checks whether a piece of research holds up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is by' only links the parts.
explanation.definitionFit: To confirm is to establish that something is true, to check and support it.

clue.text: Spoil brightly coloured feline

parts.note: to mar is to spoil
gay in its old sense means bright and showy

explanation.surface: Someone ruins a vividly patterned cat.
explanation.definitionFit: The margay is a small spotted wild cat of Central and South America.

clue.text: Worker gets 5. to look at cavity

parts.note: a worker is a kind of ant, the classic crossword insect
the answer to 5 across is a word for alcohol, and rum is one such drink

explanation.surface: A labourer is sent to inspect a hollow space.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference 5 points to SPIRIT, read here as strong drink, so it gives RUM. 'to look at' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: An antrum is a hollow or sinus in the body, especially in a bone.

clue.text: Wind to the east is rigorous

parts.note: Auster is the south wind of classical myth
E is the compass abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: An easterly wind is harsh.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' places E after the wind.
explanation.definitionFit: Austere means severe and strict, unsparing.

clue.text: Unlimited, 23 set out to meet clergyman

indicators.note: without its limits the month loses its first and last letters

parts.note: the answer to 23 down is a month, the fourth of the year

indicators.note: set out means the letters of set are laid out differently

explanation.surface: A clergyman is met by people setting out without restraint.
explanation.walkthrough: 23 is APRIL; 'Unlimited' trims it to PRI, and 'out' rearranges SET as EST.
explanation.definitionFit: A priest is an ordained minister of the church.

clue.text: Many a large zoo keeps an antelope

indicators.note: a zoo keeps animals inside it, so these words keep the answer within them

explanation.surface: Many a big zoo has an antelope in its collection.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'maNY A LArge'.
explanation.definitionFit: The nyala is a spiral-horned southern African antelope.

clue.text: A month in Capri likely to be expensive!

indicators.note: the month sits inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A month in Capri may well cost a lot.
explanation.walkthrough: The month spans 'cAPRI Likely'; 'to be expensive' completes the surface only.
explanation.definitionFit: April is the fourth calendar month.

clue.text: Girl to dilute perfume

parts.note: Rose is a girl's name
to water something down is to dilute it

explanation.surface: A young woman thins down a fragrance.
explanation.definitionFit: Rose-water is a fragrant liquid scented with rose petals, used as a scent.

clue.text: Old aircraft enters bad weather

definitions.meaning: the Hawker fighter plane of the Second World War

explanation.surface: A vintage plane flies into a storm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'enters' only links the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: One word names both the famous British wartime fighter and a severe cyclonic storm.

clue.text: Early heart transplant

indicators.note: transplanting moves things around, so the letters are relocated into a new order

explanation.surface: A heart transplant was performed ahead of schedule.
explanation.definitionFit: Rathe is an archaic or poetic adjective for coming early in the season or day.

clue.text: Support for member

parts.note: member reads as a limb, so this is a rigid brace for an injured arm or leg, not backing for a club member

explanation.surface: Someone seeks backing for a club member.
explanation.definitionFit: A splint is a rigid strip strapped to a broken limb to hold it straight.

clue.text: Senior man quick to obtain mooring rope

parts.note: the head is the senior person, as of a school
fast means quick

explanation.surface: A senior figure moves quickly to secure a line for the boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to obtain' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: A headfast is the line securing a vessel's bow to the shore.
